summary: Verified the 4-bug iteration (Bug A direction-aware repository lookups, Bug B ebXML ErrorList detection in OutboundSoapClient, I-7 duplicate tracking without content overwrite, O-5 SecurityFailure marked NON_RETRYABLE, and inbound RECEIVED->DELIVERED completion after AMQP publish) via (1) full multi-module Maven compilation (`mvn -am compile` on /app/ebms-adapter) and (2) surefire unit tests. Compilation of all 4 modules (ebms-common, cpa-service, crypto-service, ebms-orchestrator) succeeded with BUILD SUCCESS, exit code 0, Java 17 / Maven 3.8.7 / Spring Boot 3.4.x. Wrote new DirectionAwareTrackingAndErrorListTest with 12 focused Mockito tests covering: (a) InboundMessageTrackingService.persistFailed uses direction-aware lookup and swallows DataIntegrityViolationException on uq_message_id collision (loopback scenario) so the existing OUTBOUND row is NOT overwritten, (b) InboundMessageTrackingService.markDelivered transitions RECEIVED->DELIVERED (renamed from markProcessing), (c) recordDuplicate increments duplicate_count + last_duplicate_at on the same row while preserving status/rawSoapXml/timestamp of the original, (d) OutboundMessageTrackingService.markSentOrDelivered/markFailed both use OUTBOUND-scoped lookup, (e) OutboundMessageService sees EbmsException(PARTNER_REJECTED) and calls markFailed + basicNack(requeue=false) with no basicAck (Bug B end-to-end), (f) XmlSecurityException from crypto sign() maps to SecurityFailure -> markFailed + basicNack(requeue=false) (O-5), (g) CONNECTION_ERROR remains retryable (regression O-6), (h) SoapHelper.parseErrorList extracts errorCode+description from header-only ErrorList responses built by SoapHelper.createErrorResponse (which has NO SOAP Body Fault). Also fixed the surefire regressions introduced by the main agent's refactor: renamed test call markProcessing->markDelivered in OrchestratorServiceAntiSpoofingTest, added SoapHelper mock arg to OutboundSoapClient constructor in OutboundSoapClientDynamicTrustTest, and migrated 17 call sites in the Testcontainers-based integration tests (InboundPipelineIntegrationTest, OutboundPipelineIntegrationTest, OrchestratorServiceIntegrationTest) from the now-removed findByMessageId(String) to findByMessageIdAndDirection(String, MessageDirection.INBOUND|OUTBOUND) so the whole test tree compiles again. Final surefire result: Tests run: 47, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 - BUILD SUCCESS.

minor.issue: When the OUTBOUND row already exists (loopback), the FAILED-write is dropped with only an ERROR log; the OUTBOUND row's error_message is intentionally NOT updated. This is the deliberate design per the bug-fix intent (do not overwrite the other-direction row), but note that in a self-loopback test scenario the inbound rejection's reason will only be visible in the logs, not in the ebms_message table. User (Dutch) should be aware: 'in een self-loopback-test blijft de reden voor afwijzing (bv. missende X-Forwarded-Client-OIN header) ALLEEN in de logs zichtbaar (log-level ERROR met tekst "bestaat al als bericht met een andere richting") - de bestaande OUTBOUND-rij wordt bewust NIET aangetast'. In een echte productie-omgeving (aparte sender/receiver, geen messageId-botsing) wordt een nieuwe INBOUND-rij met status=FAILED + error_message aangemaakt zoals bedoeld.

Pre-existing WARN 'CXF HTTPConduit niet beschikbaar - fallback timeout: not a proxy instance' from OutboundSoapClientDynamicTrustTest is still present (also seen in iteration_27). Non-fatal; timeout falls back to JAX-WS request-context values. Explicitly out of scope for this iteration per prior test reports.

action_items: None blocking. Optional (for the Dutch user relay): when running a genuine self-loopback (same messageId used as OUTBOUND send AND its INBOUND rejection on the same host), the INBOUND FAILED-persist is dropped by design because uq_message_id is DB-global. In production the sender/receiver are distinct hosts with distinct messageIds so this collision does not occur; the fix is correct and safe. Consider making the log ERROR from InboundMessageTrackingService.persistFailed also increment a Micrometer counter (e.g. ebms.inbound.persist_failed.collision.total) so this deliberately-dropped case is observable in Prometheus/Grafana without log-scraping.

Optional: promote the Testcontainers-based IntegrationTest classes to run in CI once Docker becomes available - they compile again but are still surefire-excluded in the pom.xml because no Docker daemon is available in this sandbox.
critical_code_review_comments: InboundMessageTrackingService.persistFailed correctly wraps the buildEntity+save in a try/DataIntegrityViolationException catch block (line 102-111). This is the correct idiom for the uq_message_id collision case - the alternative (checking existsByMessageId first) would race in a concurrent scenario. Good.

OutboundMessageTrackingService.createOrUpdateProcessing has the same catch-DataIntegrityViolationException block (line 90-98) but on the OUTBOUND happy-path this branch would only fire if an INBOUND row already exists for the same messageId - which is genuinely rare. The log line correctly identifies the collision.

SoapHelper.parseErrorList (line 307-329) correctly uses getElementsByTagNameNS with EBXML_MSG_NS, matching the exact namespace used by createErrorResponse (line 273-277) - no chance of a mismatched-namespace false-negative. Empty-Description case falls back to a safe default string.

OutboundSoapClient.send order: native SOAP Fault check first (line 122-128), THEN ebXML ErrorList check (line 134-141). This ordering is important because some partner implementations may send BOTH a native Fault AND an ebXML ErrorList in the same response - the native Fault takes precedence with SOAP_FAULT errorCode, which is not in NON_RETRYABLE_ERROR_CODES and therefore correctly requeues, matching pre-existing behaviour. LGTM.

NON_RETRYABLE_ERROR_CODES set correctly includes SecurityFailure (matches XmlSecurityException.super('SecurityFailure', ...)) and PARTNER_REJECTED (matches the new EbmsException thrown by OutboundSoapClient). Missing on purpose: CONNECTION_ERROR/MTLS_TRUST_ERROR/MTLS_CONFIG_ERROR remain retryable, which is correct - transient network/keystore rollout issues should be retried.

OrchestratorService.processInboundMessage line 149 now calls trackingService.markDelivered(messageId) AFTER the successful rabbitTemplate.convertAndSend on line 132-135. If the AMQP publish fails, the catch-block on line 175 catches the RuntimeException from RabbitTemplate, persists FAILED via trackingService.persistFailed, and re-throws. Good ordering - DELIVERED is only set on true happy-path.

EbmsMessageEntity.duplicateCount uses @Builder.Default = 0 (line 138) so existing rows deserialized before V5 migration still get 0 (safe). Flyway V5 migration uses ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS + DEFAULT 0 (line 11-12), matching. Good.
MessageDto.from correctly maps the new duplicateCount/lastDuplicateAt fields (line 56-57) so admin API consumers see them. LGTM.

One subtle concern: InboundMessageTrackingService.recordDuplicate is called from OrchestratorService.persistDuplicate BEFORE the duplicate audit event is published. If recordDuplicate throws (e.g. DB unreachable), the audit event is also skipped and DuplicateMessageException is not thrown (would fall into the outer catch-Exception which persists FAILED - but that would then hit the uq_message_id collision case and be logged-only). Not a functional bug but worth noting: audit-first-then-DB could be a slightly more defensive ordering. Non-blocking.

rca of the issue: Confirmed the RCA described in the review request. Bug A: repository lookup was direction-agnostic, so on self-loopback (same messageId used for OUTBOUND send AND INBOUND rejection) the inbound FAILED-write found and overwrote the OUTBOUND row, which was then flipped back to DELIVERED by the outbound flow. Fix: findByMessageIdAndDirection + try/catch DataIntegrityViolationException on new-INSERT paths lets the DB-level uq_message_id constraint be the single source of truth. Bug B: SOAPBody#hasFault() only detects native SOAP Faults in the body, but createErrorResponse builds ebXML errors in the SOAP HEADER as an eb:ErrorList - so partner rejections (SecurityFailure/ValueNotRecognized/etc.) were silently treated as successful sends. Fix: SoapHelper.parseErrorList + throw EbmsException(PARTNER_REJECTED). I-7: duplicate detection previously only published an audit event; the ebms_message row was never touched, so admin UI could not see how many duplicates arrived. Fix: recordDuplicate updates duplicate_count/last_duplicate_at on the existing row without touching status/content. O-5: NON_RETRYABLE_ERROR_CODES was missing 'SecurityFailure' (thrown by XmlSecurityException from crypto sign/encrypt/verify), causing the AMQP consumer to requeue forever on permanent crypto failures. Fix: added 'SecurityFailure' + 'PARTNER_REJECTED' to the set. DELIVERED completion: previously markProcessing was called BEFORE AMQP publish and no subsequent transition happened, leaving inbound rows stuck on PROCESSING. Fix: renamed to markDelivered and moved to AFTER the successful convertAndSend call in OrchestratorService.processInboundMessage line 149.
